items.title: Google launches more visible links in AI Overviews and AI Mode
items.summary: Google has launched more visible links in AI Overviews and AI Mode, featuring pop-up windows on hover for desktop users that display additional website details. These changes aim to make it easier for users to access external content, potentially increasing click-through rates from Google's AI features. The update follows earlier testing and is designed to enhance engagement with web content.

items.title: AI search KPIs: Focus on inclusion, not position
items.summary: The article emphasizes that in AI search, success hinges on inclusion in the consideration set rather than top positioning, as users evaluate an average of 3.7 businesses per response and 60% decide without clicking through. It highlights how AI platforms like ChatGPT allow easier comparison of multiple options compared to Google search, shifting focus from rankings to crafting compelling messaging for better conversions. This has key implications for SEO strategies, urging a mindset shift toward content that ensures visibility and relevance in dynamic AI outputs.

items.title: Paid search click share doubles as organic clicks fall: Study
items.summary: A Similarweb study reveals that paid search click share doubled year-over-year as classic organic clicks fell across key U.S. verticals like headphones, jeans, greeting cards, and online games, driven by Google's expanded paid real estate and AI Overviews. Text ads and product listing ads (PLAs) captured up to one-third of clicks in product categories, prompting brands to boost paid investments amid declining organic visibility. This shift underscores intensified competition beyond AI features, with organic share dropping 11-23 percentage points while paid surfaces gained consistently.

items.title: Google's Jeff Dean: AI Search relies on classic ranking and retrieval
items.summary: Google's Jeff Dean explains that AI Search relies on traditional ranking and retrieval systems, where the process begins by narrowing tens of thousands of documents from the full index using lightweight methods before applying more sophisticated algorithms to select the final results for AI-generated answers. This staged pipeline emphasizes that content visibility depends on classic signals like relevance, quality, and freshness, rather than the AI model replacing them. The shift toward LLM-based representations allows matching queries to content based on topical relevance and intent, continuing Google's long-standing focus on semantic understanding and efficient indexing.

items.title: Google shifts Lookalike to AI signals in Demand Gen
items.summary: Google is shifting Lookalike audiences in Demand Gen campaigns to function as AI-driven optimization signals rather than strict targeting constraints, starting March 2026, allowing expanded reach beyond the selected similarity tiers to prioritize conversions. This change reduces advertiser control, leaning more on automation similar to Optimized Targeting, and offers an opt-out for legacy strict targeting. The update reflects broader industry trends toward AI-led audience expansion, potentially impacting campaign scale, CPA, and performance.

items.title: Simon & Schuster Secures Seven-Figure Deal for H.M. Wolfe’s Dystopian Romance Duology
items.summary: Scarlett Press executive editor Sarah McCabe and Simon Maverick editorial director Jason Pinter won North American rights at auction to H.M. Wolfe’s duology Daggermouth and Python in a seven-figure deal, covering print, e-book, and audio rights. The dystopian romance series, originally self-published, is set to launch in September 2026 with the second book in 2027. This reflects growing Big Five interest in new adult crossover fiction.

items.title: Mary Kubica’s Psychological Thriller 'It's Not Her' Debuts at #3 on Hardcover Fiction Bestsellers
items.summary: Mary Kubica’s new psychological thriller, It's Not Her, rocketed to the #3 spot on the hardcover fiction bestseller list just one day after publication. The novel has already caught Hollywood's eye, with Gaumont—the production company behind Lupin and Narcos—optioning it for TV series development. This marks a strong start for Kubica's latest suspense hit.

items.title: Shannon J. Spann’s YA Fantasy Debuts at #11 on Children’s Fiction List
items.summary: Shannon J. Spann enters the children’s fiction bestseller list at #11 with her YA fantasy novel, a dark and propulsive homage to theater. The book employs scriptlike dialogue and dramatic structures to build a vivid world around the Playhouse. Drawing from her background as a former high school theater kid, Spann highlights theater's appeal to misfits.

items.title: Grand Central Preempts Cecily von Ziegesar’s Return to Gossip Girl Universe with 'Blair'
items.summary: Grand Central preempted world rights to Blair, a standalone novel by Gossip Girl creator Cecily von Ziegesar, set 20 years after the original series. The story follows Blair Waldorf’s return to New York City and her quest to reclaim her spot at the top of Upper East Side society. Publication is slated for summer 2027.

items.title: New Sci-Fi Novella 'The Rainseekers' Hits Shelves February 17
items.summary: In this science fiction novella, has-been influencer Sakunja struggles to maintain her photography job on Mars while her team ventures into dangerous terrain to capture the planet’s historic first rain. The story explores themes of redemption and survival in a harsh extraterrestrial environment. It's one of the notable speculative releases this week.

items.title: NPR Spotlights 7 Must-See Spring Movies Including Sci-Fi Book Adaptation 'Project Hail Mary'
items.summary: NPR has highlighted seven anticipated movies for spring 2026, featuring the sci-fi book adaptation 'Project Hail Mary' starring Ryan Gosling as a lone astronaut saving Earth, releasing March 20. Other key releases include the Star Wars film 'The Mandalorian and Grogu' on May 22 and Pixar's mind-transfer adventure 'Hoppers' on March 6. The list also covers sequels like 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' and unique tales such as 'The Sheep Detectives'.

items.title: KOMO News Lists 7 Most Anticipated Book-to-Film Adaptations of 2026
items.summary: KOMO News recently shared their top seven book adaptations for 2026, kicking off with Andy Weir's 'Project Hail Mary' starring Ryan Gosling on March 10, followed by Homer's 'The Odyssey' in July with an all-star cast including Matt Damon and Zendaya. Highlights also include the fantasy sequel 'Practical Magic 2' with Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman in September, 'Sunrise on the Reaping' Hunger Games prequel, and 'Dune: Part 3'. Sci-fi and fantasy dominate the exciting lineup.

items.title: Collider Announces 'The Green Knight' Dark Fantasy Streaming on Netflix March 2026
items.summary: David Lowery's critically acclaimed dark fantasy 'The Green Knight', starring Dev Patel as a questing knight, will begin streaming on Netflix March 1, 2026. Hailed as a genre-redefining film comparable to 'Game of Thrones', it boasts an 89% Rotten Tomatoes score for subverting tropes despite modest box office. The 130-minute epic challenges masculinity and fantasy conventions.

items.title: BookTrib's Most Anticipated Book-to-Screen Adaptations for 2026 Feature Wuthering Heights and Project Hail Mary
items.summary: BookTrib outlines key 2026 adaptations, starting with Emily Brontë's gothic 'Wuthering Heights' starring Margot Robbie and Jacob Elordi, released February 13. Sci-fi standout 'Project Hail Mary' with Ryan Gosling follows on March 20, alongside fantasy entries like 'Remarkably Bright Creatures' and 'The Book of Magic' starring Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock. These films promise emotional depth across genres.

items.title: The Reality of AI’s Impact on Small Businesses: New Evidence from Gusto Payroll Data
items.summary: Gusto's analysis of payroll data from over 400,000 small businesses shows that higher AI exposure in the workforce leads to revenue gains, with a 10-percentage-point increase predicting 2.2% higher monthly revenue—about $53,800 annually for a typical firm—and slight employment growth rather than job losses. AI adoption has stabilized around 16%, enhancing productivity within existing roles like copywriting and customer service. Younger workers in AI-exposed jobs face challenges, potentially driving more Gen Z entrepreneurship.

items.title: Small Business Technology News: AI Models That Are Better Than ChatGPT
items.summary: Intuit is expanding its AI and fintech offerings for small businesses, integrating Affirm financing, Checkr background checks, and OpenAI’s Frontier AI into QuickBooks to streamline financial operations. LinkedIn's new agentic AI Hiring Assistant automates multi-step recruitment tasks, saving recruiters up to four hours per role. Newo.ai raised $25M to build voice and text AI agents as virtual front-desk assistants for SMBs, handling calls, chats, and appointments.

items.title: Cantwell, Moran Reintroduce Bill to Help Small Business Leverage AI Tools
items.summary: U.S. Senators Cantwell and Moran reintroduced the bipartisan Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026, authorizing the Department of Commerce and SBA to create AI training resources and toolkits for small businesses. The bill focuses on practical applications in financial management, marketing, supply chains, and government contracting, delivered through SBA partners like Small Business Development Centers. This aims to equip entrepreneurs with AI skills to compete, innovate, and grow.

items.title: Why Agentic AI Is Breaking The SaaS Pricing Model
items.summary: Agentic AI systems, which autonomously handle tasks and evolve, are disrupting traditional SaaS pricing by making user-based 'seats' obsolete and shifting to metrics like transactions or compute usage with dynamic fees. Small business owners may face more complex pricing structures resembling software-as-a-service hybrids with built-in consulting. This evolution requires entrepreneurs to better understand value delivery to manage costs effectively.
